reaction.episode: CORRECTION episode through Friday Nov 20: SPX 6,910.39, -11.91% from its 120-day high, -9.37% below its 50-day and -5.96% below its 200-day; SMH 400.06 and NVDA 125.53 both BELOW Zone 2; VIX 35.89 on Friday (26.9 midday Monday); HY OAS 3.76, credit calm; mechanical capitulation tally 1 of 4. Monday's +4.61% SPY / +30.53% NVDA bounce is the first bounce — unconfirmed, with no second low and no failure-zone test yet. Episode data is fresh (through Nov 20 close).
reaction.invalidation: A held weekly close above the failure zone (SPX 7,750-7,820, SMH 580-600) with the mechanical tally at 3 of 4 or better and HY OAS contained below 4.00% would void the Watch stance — the correction would be over and the ladder's re-entry condition met.

ladder.response: Regime break confirmed — stand down on all new deployment, keep new money in bills, and re-grade the thesis from the break, not the dip.
ladder.trigger: SPX closes a second week below 7,000, or HY OAS closes above 4.00%.

ladder.response: Trap confirmed — do not chase the first bounce; any probe waits for the failure-zone retest verdict and a second low that holds.
ladder.trigger: Bounce carries SPX into the 7,750-7,820 failure zone or SMH into 580-600 and fails there.

ladder.response: Bounce failed at the first test — the correction extends toward the next zone down; no entries, watch for the second low forming.
ladder.trigger: SPX loses Friday's close of 6,910.39 and closes below it.

ladder.response: Confirmed-bottom condition met — re-entry arms under the deployment ladder, starting with the Zone 2 prints (SMH $470-505, NVDA $175-185).
ladder.trigger: Failed first bounce, then a second low that holds while the 10-year falls, or a held weekly close above SPX 7,750-7,820 / SMH 580-600.

reaction.trapRisk: Today's +4.61% SPY / +30.53% NVDA move is exactly the shape of a pivot-and-fail: a violent one-day bounce inside an unconfirmed correction (tally 1 of 4, both SMH and NVDA still below Zone 2). Entries do not chase it — no probe until the bounce either holds above Friday's close through the weekly close or fails and prints a second low that holds. The trap case is buying the bounce into the 7,750-7,820 failure zone and holding through the rejection.

strategyPosture: Watch. The tape printed its first bounce after a seven-session slide (SPX -8.61% in five days), but the mechanical tally is 1 of 4, SMH and NVDA remain below Zone 2, and no bottom has been confirmed — nothing is bought on a one-day +30% move.

themes.counterRead: The rotation read holds only while credit stays loose. If lending standards tighten toward 40% or HY OAS breaks 4.00%, the same divergence becomes a rollover in retrospect. The divergence is real and worth tracking; it is not yet a verdict on the broad market.
themes.dataAnchor: Mag7 averages -19.07% from 52-week highs versus SPY at -7.5% — an 11.57-point divergence gap, with NVDA weakest at -32.6% and AAPL strongest at -3.2%. Bank lending standards are LOOSE at 1.7% (SLOOS), far below the ~40% stress threshold. SPX itself is -11.91% from its 120-day high: a correction, with leadership rotating out of the concentrated names rather than credit forcing a broad unwind.
themes.label: Index rotation, not rollover
themes.narrative: The Mag7-led selloff reads as a broad market rollover — the names that carried the index are the ones falling hardest, so the whole tape must be breaking.
themes.watchFor: SLOOS lending standards rising toward 40% or HY OAS closing above 4.00%.

themes.counterRead: Revenue growth does not clear the governance and financing questions — the SEC probe and customer-financing scrutiny are real and unresolved, and NVDA's -14.01% day on Friday shows the market is still repricing them. The gap is an opportunity only for names whose demand is verified; the rest of the complex is a falling knife until the probe and the financing story resolve.
themes.dataAnchor: NVDA revenue is growing 61.4% YoY while the stock sits -32.6% from its high and -48.42% from its 120-day high; AVGO +55% YoY at -37.4% from its high; DDOG +27.7% YoY at -44.1% from its high with 80% gross margin and $1,001M free cash flow; ONTO +41.5% YoY at -50.3% from its high; PLTR +56.2% YoY at -26.1% from its high. The 36-name dislocation list is dominated by SENTIMENT_DRIVEN declines — only NVDA and PLTR carry an ACUTE_CATALYST flag. The screened conviction set (DDOG 82, AVGO 82, ONTO 81; promotions ETN 85, KTOS 80) is where the gap is cleanest.
themes.label: AI infrastructure: revenue ahead of price
themes.narrative: The AI trade is dead — the accounting probe, the CEO exit, and the circular-financing revelations mean the whole AI capex story was a bubble and the stocks should keep falling.
themes.watchFor: NVDA reclaiming Zone 2 ($175-185) and holding it on a weekly close.

themes.counterRead: A one-day +30% in NVDA and +18.42% in TQQQ is a short-covering-shaped move, not a confirmed bottom — there has been no failed first bounce and no second low that holds. Chasing it repeats the error of buying the first bounce in every prior leg of this drawdown; the bounce is a test to watch, not a signal to buy.
themes.dataAnchor: The bounce comes after SPX fell -8.61% in five sessions and -9.36% in twenty, closing Friday at 6,910.39, -9.37% below its 50-day and -5.96% below its 200-day. The mechanical capitulation tally is 1 of 4 — only credit calm is confirmed; zone occupancy, volume-climax reversal, and VIX rollover are all unconfirmed. VIX was 35.89 on Friday and is 26.9 at midday, still +38.3% over one month. SMH closed Friday at 400.06, below its Zone 2 floor of $470; NVDA closed Friday at 125.53, below its Zone 2 floor of $175 — even after today's +30.53%, NVDA is about $164, still below Zone 2.
themes.label: First bounce, unconfirmed
themes.narrative: Monday's tape says the bottom is in — SPY +4.61%, QQQ +6.7%, NVDA +30.53% in a single session, so the correction is over.
themes.watchFor: Whether the bounce holds above Friday's close (SPX 6,910.39) through the weekly close, or fails back below it.

themes.counterRead: HY OAS at 3.76 is 24bp from the line, and widening is the trend to watch, not the level — a calm reading today can flip fast if the equity bounce fails. The re-entry condition requires the 10-year falling alongside a held second low; neither has printed.
themes.dataAnchor: HY OAS is 3.76, below the 4.00% stand-down line, and the episode block marks credit calm: true, cracking: false. Lending standards are loose at 1.7%. But the 10-year is 5.04% with a 2s10s of +0.28 and a real 10-year of 2.89% — rates, not credit, are the binding constraint, and the 10-year has not fallen.
themes.label: Credit calm, rates still the ceiling
themes.narrative: Credit is about to break — the AI unwind will take the credit market with it and force a deeper leg down.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS closing above 4.00%, or the 10-year rising while equities retest Friday's lows.

themes.counterRead: The unwind is mechanical — leveraged products decay in a drawdown — not new information about the underlying. The sleeve (CONL, BMNR, DOGE) stays in a watch posture; the dislocation is the product structure, not a buy signal, and the same leverage that fell -59.61% in a month can give back a one-day +11.86% just as fast.
themes.dataAnchor: BTC-USD is -20.02% over one month, but the leveraged proxies have fallen far further: CONL -59.61%, BMNR -35.2%, COIN -34.13%, IBIT -24.49%, DOGE -22.98%. Today's bounce is equally outsized in the same names (CONL +11.86%, BMNR +11.83%), which is leverage working in both directions.
themes.label: Leveraged crypto proxies unwind faster than crypto
themes.narrative: Crypto is collapsing and taking the leveraged proxies down with it — the whole sleeve is broken.
themes.watchFor: CONL or BMNR making a new low while BTC-USD holds flat — that would signal forced selling, not price discovery.

watchFor: SPX weekly close vs 6,910.39 (Friday's close) — a hold keeps the bounce alive; a second close below 7,000 confirms the regime break.
NVDA reclaiming and holding Zone 2 ($175-185) on a weekly close — about $164 after Monday's +30.53% bounce, still below the zone.
HY OAS closing above 4.00% (now 3.76) — the credit-break line.
VIX rolling over from its 35.89 five-day high and closing below 25 — currently 26.9 at midday.
SMH reclaiming Zone 2 ($470-505) — closed Friday at 400.06, below the zone.
whereWaveBuilds: The next move is decided at the failure zone: either the bounce carries SPX toward 7,750-7,820 and SMH toward 580-600 and fails there (the trap), or it fails first at Friday's close of 6,910.39 and the correction extends toward the next zone down. The trigger is the weekly close — a hold above 6,910.39 keeps the bounce alive; a second close below 7,000 confirms the regime break.
